page: Amazon Web Services c8ib.4xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by x86_64 Intel processors running at a sustained clock speed of 3.9 GHz, the instance delivers 16 vCPUs mapped across 8 physical cores with dedicated thread execution. Memory allocation is balanced for compute-heavy requirements, providing 32.0 GB of system RAM, which evaluates to a standard compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

Network connectivity features a baseline throughput of 17 Gbps, facilitating reliable communication for distributed nodes and backend application layers. The instance does not include bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions for all persistence needs. Accelerated computing components are absent, with no GPUs available on this hardware configuration.

From an efficiency standpoint, the c8ib.4xlarge targets compute-intensive workloads that prioritize clock speed over high memory densities or local disk I/O. Typical workload profiles suitable for this server include batch computing jobs, continuous integration and build pipelines, distributed microservices, media transcoding, and high-traffic web serving.
description: Amazon Web Services c8ib.4xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and dedicated 3.9 GHz Intel x86_64 processors. It is configured with 16 vCPUs across 8 physical cores and 32.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 compute-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance incorporates a 17 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, while containing no integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators. Architecturally suited for CPU-dominated tasks, c8ib.4xlarge provides reliable per-core throughput for workloads such as code compilation, CI/CD processing pipelines, web serving clusters, and batch processing nodes that do not mandate high RAM capacity.
